summary: Durham County Council manages demand in the historic city mainly through price and access rules. The Road User Charge zone on the peninsula is shown on the council's undated page (read 21 October 2026) as £5 a day between 10am and 2am, Monday to Sunday, with an ANPR camera at Silver Street and Claypath; a January 2025 student-newspaper report described the rise from £2, Sunday charging and longer hours as a council proposal. A 2023 delegated-decision report and a February 2024 Highways Committee meeting dealt with extending on-street pay and display charging to Sundays (8am to 6pm) with a 20p an hour rise, the income to fund a Sunday Park and Ride service; the committee endorsed this in principle, and no source opened confirms the final decision or the in-force date. The Controlled Parking Zone needs a permit from 8am to 6pm every day including most bank holidays, with resident permits at £56 and £84 a year. A March 2026 Local Democracy Reporting Service story (carried on AOL) said council leaders had approved rises from the following month of 30p an hour off-street and 15p an hour on-street in Durham's council car parks and 4p per permit per day; a notice dated 14 May 2026 varied the Sands and Sidegate tariffs to £2.10 for up to two hours then £1.10 an hour from 4 June 2026, Providence Row to 55p per half hour and Wharton Park to 80p per half hour, and a June 2026 notice proposed amending the on-street orders so that Good Friday and bank holidays would no longer be excluded. Park and Ride is the main alternative: Sniperley was expanded by 261 bays to 587 in November 2024, Belmont has 533 spaces and Howlands Farm 361, with an adult day pass of £2.20; the council says Belmont and Sniperley run seven days and Howlands Monday to Saturday, although the Cathedral's own page says all three run Monday to Saturday. The council lists Prince Bishops, The Riverwalk, Walkergate and the LNER station as third-party car parks with no spaces or charges given. Developer plans reported in February 2026 would keep the Prince Bishops Place multi-storey car park under around 500 student rooms, subject to a new planning application. An August 2026 order set a £1 an hour charge from 8am to 8pm for off-street parking at The Light, although its notice gives an inconsistent start date. A July 2024 report said the council and Zest would install 250 charging locations across the county, and the hospital trust announced number-plate recognition at University Hospital North Durham from 1 May 2025.

items.text: In January 2025 Durham County Council was reported to be proposing to raise the Road User Charge for the Durham peninsula from £2 to £5 a day, to charge on Sundays and bank holidays (except Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day) and to extend enforcement from 10am-4pm to 10am-2am. The council cited disruptive parking, safety and air pollution, and said up to 30,000 vehicles pass through the area each month; the City of Durham Parish Council was reviewing the plans.
items.source_title: Durham County Council Proposes Changes to Road User Charge (Palatinate)

items.text: As shown on the council's Road User Charge Zone page when read on 21 October 2026 (the page carries no date), the charge is £5 a day for using the zone between 10am and 2am, Monday to Sunday, except Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day. An ANPR camera at Silver Street and Claypath records vehicles, payment is up to 2 weeks ahead or within 24 hours, and an unpaid charge can bring a £50 Penalty Charge Notice.
items.source_title: Durham Road User Charge Zone (Durham County Council)

items.text: A November 2023 delegated-decision report said the council had proposed a revised parking strategy in which availability of spaces together with price is the main driver of modal shift. It proposed Sunday tariffs on all Durham City on-street pay-and-display bays, estimated at £119,890 extra income a year, with on-street charging then running 8am to 6pm on all days; it noted that charging had been Monday to Saturday since on-street charges began on 5 May 2003.
items.source_title: Delegated Decision, Durham City (North East) Parking & Waiting Restrictions TRO 2024 (REG 2408)

items.text: On 20 February 2024 the council's Highways Committee endorsed in principle the Durham City parking orders, which proposed Sunday on-street operation from 8am to 6pm and a 20p per hour tariff rise, with the extra income to fund a Sunday Park and Ride service. The officers' presentation said free Sunday bays were being filled by long-stay parkers and that queues had been seen at city-centre private car parks, and recorded public objections citing cost of living, effects on businesses and falling visitor numbers.
items.source_title: Highways Committee 20 February 2024, item 5 and officers' presentation (Durham City Parking Place TRO 2024)

items.text: On 23 March 2026 the Local Democracy Reporting Service (carried on AOL) reported that Durham County Council leaders had approved parking increases 'next month' (April 2026): 30p an hour for off-street and 15p an hour for on-street parking in council-run car parks in Durham, and 10p an hour in all on- and off-street council car parks in Barnard Castle, Bishop Auckland, Chester-le-Street and Seaham. Permit prices were to rise by 4p per permit per day, which a councillor had described as the first increase in permit charges since 2015, and the permit rise was estimated to bring in an additional £400,000. The council said its city centre parking charges were competitive compared with private sector operators in Durham and elsewhere in the North East.
items.source_title: County-wide parking charge increase from April (Local Democracy Reporting Service, via AOL)

items.text: A notice dated 14 May 2026 varied the Durham City off-street order with effect from 4 June 2026: Sidegate and The Sands multi-storey move from £1.80 for 0-2 hours then 80p an hour to £2.10 then £1.10 an hour (8am-10pm), and Providence Row from 40p to 55p per half hour (8am-6pm). The council's Durham City car parks page lists the same new tariffs.
items.source_title: Notice of Variation of Parking Charges, Durham City (Off-Street Parking Places) Order 2008, Variation No. 1 (2026)

items.text: A notice for Wharton Park, Durham, varied its charge from 70p to 80p per half hour from 4 June 2026, for all days 8am to 6pm with a 3-hour maximum stay. The council lists Wharton Park as a 25-space car park with 2 EV points that accepts cash and PayByPhone only.
items.source_title: Wharton Park, Durham: Variation of Off-Street Parking Charges (Variation No 1, 2026)

items.text: The council's Durham City car parks page (undated, read 21 October 2026) lists four council pay-and-display sites: The Sands multi-storey (277 spaces, 14 x 7kW EV points), Sidegate (107 spaces, 2 x 22kW), Providence Row (19) and Wharton Park (25). It lists Prince Bishops, The Riverwalk, Walkergate and LNER Durham station as third-party car parks and gives no spaces or charges for them.
items.source_title: Durham City car parks (Durham County Council)

items.text: The £2 million expansion of Sniperley Park and Ride, funded through the Transforming Cities Fund, was announced complete on 19 November 2024. It added 261 bays to a total of 587, including 28 disabled bays, 14 EV bays, 2 accessible EV bays and 3 motorhome bays.
items.source_title: Expansion of Sniperley Park and Ride complete (Durham County Council)

items.text: The council's Belmont Park and Ride page (undated, read 21 October 2026) lists 533 spaces including 12 disabled bays, and 8 EV points (2 x 7.4kW, 4 x 22kW, 2 x 50kW). The car park is open 7am to 7pm, Monday to Sunday including bank holidays (except Christmas Day, Boxing Day and New Year's Day), with buses every 15 minutes. The adult day pass is £2.20 and the Pop pay-as-you-go day pass is £2. The £1.10 Durham University student fare applies only when boarding at Howlands. Overnight motorhome parking is £5 a night for a maximum of two consecutive nights, 7pm to 7am.
items.source_title: Belmont Park and Ride (Durham County Council)

items.text: The council's Howlands Farm Park and Ride page (undated, read 21 October 2026) lists 361 spaces including 12 disabled bays and 4 x 7.4kW EV points. It is open 7am to 7pm Monday to Saturday only and is closed on bank holidays, with buses every 15 minutes, Monday to Saturday. The adult day pass is £2.20.
items.source_title: Howlands Farm Park and Ride (Durham County Council)

items.text: A notice dated 13 August 2026 reported a Durham County Council order, made 7 August 2026, for off-street parking at The Light, Durham (DH1 5TU), with a charge of £1 an hour from 8am to 8pm on all days, EV charging bays, staff and visitor permits and a cashless payment service. The notice gives an inconsistent in-force date (4/7/2024), so the start date is unclear.
items.source_title: The County Council of Durham (The Light, Durham) (Off-Street Parking Places) Order 2026

items.text: On 8 July 2024 Place North East reported that Durham County Council had approved the Prince Bishops Place redevelopment by Citrus Group in joint venture with Galliard Homes, a scheme of shops and leisure uses, public space, a hotel and student accommodation, with the well-used multi-storey car park to be retained. At that date work was expected to start on site in mid-2025, with the student housing opening in autumn 2028.
items.source_title: Green light for Prince Bishops Place redevelopment (Place North East)

items.text: On 2 February 2026 Place North East reported revised Prince Bishops Place plans: the approved hotel is dropped, student accommodation rises to around 500 rooms above the car park and retail units, and the existing multi-storey car park stays. A new planning application was expected by the end of February 2026; the report gives no space numbers.
items.source_title: Citrus revises Prince Bishops Place plans (Place North East)

items.text: County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust announced on 23 April 2025 that from 1 May 2025 the University Hospital North Durham visitor car park would use number-plate recognition with no entry ticket. Drivers get 20 minutes to find a space, pay by registration at a machine, then have 20 minutes to leave; Blue Badge holders park free in designated bays, and the patient section has 11 EV charge points.
items.source_title: Changes to parking at University Hospital North Durham: what you need to know when visiting (CDDFT)

items.text: The council's Durham City Controlled Parking Zone page (undated, read 21 October 2026) says a permit is needed from 8am to 6pm, Monday to Sunday including bank holidays, and parking is free outside those hours. It lists resident permits at £56 a year for the first and £84 for the second (maximum two per household), business permits at £500 a year and visitor vouchers at £12 per block of 36 three-hour vouchers.
items.source_title: Durham City Controlled Parking Zone (CPZ) (Durham County Council)

items.text: A notice published 11 June 2026 proposed amendments to four Durham City on-street parking orders (North East, North West, South West, South East) to change which holidays are excluded from bay restrictions: Good Friday and bank holidays removed from the exemption list and Boxing Day added. Objections were invited from 11 June to 2 July 2026; the notice gives no charge amounts or in-force date.
items.source_title: Durham - Amendments to Parking & Waiting Restrictions & Parking Charge Exemptions (public notice)

items.text: On 21 July 2024 ElectricDrives reported that Durham County Council and charge-point operator Zest would install 250 new charging locations across County Durham, with over £11 million of combined funding (£4 million from the government's LEVI scheme and £7 million from Zest), aimed at the 40% of residents without driveways, with installation due to begin in September 2024. The article does not mention Durham city specifically.
items.source_title: County Durham set for electric boost with 250 new Zest charge points (ElectricDrives)

gaps: No dated source opened for when the Road User Charge actually rose to £5: the council RUC page is undated, the 6 May 2025 council post on X (https://x.com/DurhamCouncil/status/1918198776436789288) returned HTTP 402, and the Palatinate article (Jan 2025) describes only a proposal

No opened source for the actual in-force Sunday on-street charging or a Sunday Park and Ride service: the Feb 2024 committee endorsed it in principle, but the council's Park and Ride pages show Howlands Monday to Saturday only and Belmont and Sniperley seven days; Durham Cathedral's page (https://www.durhamcathedral.co.uk/visit-us/plan-your-visit/parking-getting-to-durham-cathedral) says all three run Monday to Saturday, a conflict with the council pages

No opened source on tariffs, operators or ownership for the third-party car parks (Prince Bishops, Walkergate, Riverwalk, LNER station); the only tariffs seen were third-party listings and a 2022 cathedral document, which were not used. No opened source on NCP, APCOA or Q-Park in Durham city (the council page lists no such operators)

No opened source for Salvus House, Sherburn Road or Gilesgate car park schemes, Milburngate multi-storey capacity, or Aykley Heads (county HQ redevelopment) parking numbers; no Durham-specific Clean Air Zone or low-emission zone found; no stand-alone 'Durham parking strategy' document found beyond the 2023 delegated-decision report

The Light order notice gives a conflicting in-force date (4/7/2024) against an order made 7/8/2026, and the sealed order was not opened; the site's relationship to Milburngate is not stated in any opened source

Two Durham County Council committee PDFs (Highways Committee presentation and REG 2408) were read from locally decoded text; REG 2408 pages 5 to 16 are map extracts only. Durham Pointers (https://www.durhampointers.co.uk/explore/parking-in-durham), a visitor guide, was opened but not used as support because it is an unofficial guide with an unclear date

LEVI/Zest charge-point numbers actually live in Durham city, and the Durham County Council own-site EV tariff, were not found; Durham World Heritage Site restriction documents were not found beyond the Road User Charge
